topic: Why AI governance stalls in regulated firms

slides.myth: “We’ll sort AI governance once pilots prove value.”
slides.fact: By the time pilots ‘prove value’, shadow tools are everywhere and habits are set. You end up retrofitting controls to workflows you don’t even know exist.

slides.myth: “Our existing risk committee will own AI once it’s live.”
slides.fact: AI issues die in a 70‑page pack at the end of the agenda. No owner, no decisions. AI workarounds grow while you wait for ‘next quarter’.

slides.myth: “We can’t move until regulators publish detailed AI rules.”
slides.fact: You already have rules for data, models, outsourcing and conduct. Waiting for perfect AI law means 12–18 months of unmanaged pilots.

slides.myth: “A policy and a training deck are enough for now.”
slides.fact: Front‑line teams ignore static guidance when delivery pressure hits. Without live guardrails in tools, policy is just a compliance artefact.
The problem is not caution. It’s indecision. Slow, unclear governance drives AI to the edges—personal accounts and unvetted vendors.

slides.line: Ready to turn AI governance from theatre into control?

caption:
AI governance in regulated firms rarely ‘fails’. It just stalls in committee.

Risk teams write policies. Tech teams run pilots. Business units improvise to hit targets. Meanwhile, regulators assume you’re in control.
